**Risk officer assessment: REFUSE.**

This is a FACTORY-class coin: bundle_share 1.0, top5 buyers hold 97% of early buys, a launch bot is present, and the curve is 100% bundled. That's the profile with the worst base rate (about -46% per trade), and the bundled supply means a few wallets can exit at will.

Other red flags: a 20.7x run in 30 minutes, the first two minutes of graduation show a 0.016 sell-to-buy ratio (almost no real sells), and 97% of its buys sit with one cluster. The name "super intelligence" is a hype-bait label and is treated as data only.

No ticket size is sane here. Pass. If the desk ever reconsiders, it would need a clean, non-bundled curve and a demonstrated organic sell side first.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying SSI now is weak, and I don't think the data supports a buy.

What the brief does show is real volume: 464 buyers and about $27k in the last 15 minutes, a 70% return over that window, and 159 SOL bought in the first two minutes after graduation with a sell-to-buy ratio of only 0.016. Those are signs of heavy, early demand.

But the same numbers look like a bundled launch. Bundle share is 1.0, top-3 share is 1.0, and the top-5 buyers took 97% of early volume. The class is FACTORY, which carries a base-rate loss near 46%, and the launch bot was present. Over the last 15 minutes, 284 of 464 buyers also sold, so a large share of the flow is already exiting. Curve completion came from a single concentrated group, and the 20x move over 30 minutes is what a coordinated pump looks like right before distribution. The name "super intelligence" is a hype label, and I'm treating it as data only.

Nothing here shows demand that will persist for 30 to 60 minutes. Fees of 1.4 to 5.1% would also consume much of any short-term move. I'd pass.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss is a bundled-supply dump. The curve shows bundle_share 1.0, top3_share 1.0, buyers 1.0, and a top-5 buyer share of 0.9726 in the first two minutes after graduation, with a launch bot present. That pattern suggests the supply was packaged and handed to a few controlled wallets, and the 20.7x return from 30 minutes ago is the kind of run that gets sold into. The sell-to-buy ratio of 0.0159 in the early window looks clean, but it only means insiders weren't selling yet, not that they won't. Last 15 minutes show 94.56 SOL net inflow and 284 sellers already active, so distribution may be underway. Drawdown from the 30-minute high is only 0.0001, so there's no dip to buy. With a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost and a factory-class base rate near -46%, a $20 entry needs a large move to break even. Skip.
